# Elastic is a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave™ for AIOps Platforms, Q4 2026


Open architecture, explainable AI, and full context


By


[Natalie Blake](https://www.elastic.co/blog/author/natalie-blake)


October 28, 2026

Elastic was named a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave™: AIOps Platforms, Q4 2026, which evaluated 10 providers across 24 criteria. Forrester gave Elastic the highest possible scores in five criteria: algorithmic trust and explainability, observability as code (OaC) and GitOps alignment, AI stack and semantic observability, sovereign deployment and data isolation, and pricing flexibility and transparency. We believe these strengths support how we built AIOps into an


[AI SRE](https://www.elastic.co/observability/ai-sre) that shows its evidence, learns from every investigation, and finds what alerts miss.


## Why incident response needs a different kind of help


In our view, the AI conversation in operations has moved on from whether a model can propose a root cause. The question teams ask now is whether they can rely on the answer. Telemetry keeps growing, code is generating code, and AI-based components make failures harder to predict. We believe the answer comes down to transparency, learning, context, and openness. Here is what sets our approach apart.


### Trust starts with evidence


An AI recommendation is only as reliable as an engineer’s ability to check it.


We built


[Elastic nightshift AI SRE](https://www.elastic.co/observability/ai-sre) as an always-on AI coworker that investigates like an engineer. It lays out its reasoning, what data it looked at, which explanations it considered, and what evidence supports the conclusion. SRE teams can follow the investigation from the start and confirm it before they approve an action.


### Context that stays complete


AI can only reason over the data it can reach. Many teams cut telemetry to control costs, which means the evidence an investigation needs may no longer exist when the incident arrives. In our view, teams shouldn’t have to choose between affordability and fast, accurate incident resolutions. Elastic is built with cost-efficient storage for


[logs, traces,](https://www.elastic.co/observability-labs/blog/elasticsearch-logsdb-index-mode-storage-savings) and


[metrics](https://www.elastic.co/elasticsearch/metrics) so they can keep all their data in one place and give AI the full picture to work from. What’s more, Elastic distills what’s actually relevant about the environment into


[compact context](https://www.elastic.co/observability-labs/blog/elastic-knowledge-indicators-log-extraction) for the SRE agent to reason over, improving both accuracy and token-efficiency.


### AI that learns and looks ahead


Each investigation should leave the system better informed. Elastic’s AI SRE carries what it learns from past incidents into the next one, so a problem that returns is recognized sooner and its recommendations improve over time.


Detection based on alerts only covers failures that can be predicted. Elastic is built for the incidents that break your assumptions, surfacing what else deserves attention, including the unknown unknowns that you can’t write a rule for.


### Open standards that keep your options open


Observability tooling changes quickly, and closed stacks make every change expensive. Elastic is open by design and built on


[OpenTelemetry](https://www.elastic.co/observability/opentelemetry) . We keep data in its native form, so teams can adopt new instrumentation without rebuilding pipelines or translating schemas. The investment in your data holds up as the ecosystem moves.


## What this recognition means to us


We believe being named a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave™: AIOps Platforms, Q4 2026 reflects what engineers want from AI in operations: answers they can verify, context that isn’t limited by what they can afford to store, and the freedom to build on open standards.


These connect: efficient storage makes complete context possible, complete context makes AI investigations accurate, transparent reasoning makes them checkable, and open standards keep the investment portable.
